changed.title: A linear gate lower bound for fan-in-two AND/OR circuits selecting complements of four-cycle-free graphs
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  let nbrR := fun (sourceRow : Fin n) => Finset.univ.filter (fun destCol : Fin m => G sourceRow destCol = false)
  let nbrC := fun (sourceCol : Fin m) => Finset.univ.filter (fun destRow : Fin n => G destRow sourceCol = false)
  (∀ a, 2 ≤ (nbrR a).card) → (∀ c, 2 ≤ (nbrC c).card) →
  (∀ a b, a ≠ b → ((nbrR a) ∩ (nbrR b)).card ≤ 1) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  13 * (n + m) ≤ 12 * C.size + 18 ∧
  ((∀ a, 3 ≤ (nbrR a).card) → (∀ c, 3 ≤ (nbrC c).card) →
    13 * (n + m) ≤ 12 * C.size + 14)
changed.unlocks: bounds the total number of AND/OR gates for zero graphs of minimum degree two or three
changed.context: Every raw input is used. When N≥19 at most two vertices have at most three positive partners. Two such rows share two zero columns if m≥8. For a smaller bank count the disjoint row pairs used by columns. Only n=6,7 need checking. With H shared inputs, P shared gates and D excess reads, H+P≤D. Disjoint forest regions charge N≤H+2(2P+1+4D)+4≤12D+6. Substitute s=N−1+D. For N from 7 to 18 at least one shared wire is needed. Degree three removes both exception charges.

changed.title: A fan-in-two circuit counts distinct keys meeting one-round targets with size exponential only in the rank of the quadratic parts
changed.statement:
∀ (k m t q : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k),
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let X := Fin m → ZMod 2
  let ix := fun pos : ℕ => (⟨pos % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (j : Fin k) => w (ix (j.val+k-s%k))
  let run := fun (d s f : ℕ) (w name c : W) =>
    let z := rot s w + name
    let y := fun mid : Fin k => z mid + z (ix (mid.val+d)) + z (ix (mid.val+k-d%k))
    fun siteOut : Fin k => y siteOut + (1+y (ix (siteOut.val+1))) * y (ix (siteOut.val+2)) + rot f w siteOut + c siteOut
  ∀ (site : Fin t → Fin k) (column : Fin t → Bool),
    let inputs := (m+5)*k+t
    ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (out : Fin (k+1) → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
      C.size ≤ 2^20*(k+m+t+2)^8*2^(min q t) ∧
      ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (u v cr cc : W) (target : Fin t → ZMod 2),
        let key := fun a : X => base + ∑ j : Fin m, a j • gen j
        let probe := fun (w : W) (j : Fin t) =>
          if column j then run 2 3 4 w v cc (site j) else run 1 1 0 w u cr (site j)
        let unit := fun (j i : Fin m) => (if i = j then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2)
        let H : Matrix (Fin t) (Fin m × Fin m) (ZMod 2) := fun obs ab =>
          probe (key (unit ab.1 + unit ab.2)) obs + probe (key (unit ab.1)) obs +
          probe (key (unit ab.2)) obs + probe (key 0) obs
        let pack := fun (word : W) => List.ofFn (fun bitIndex : Fin k => decide (word bitIndex ≠ 0))
        let bits := pack base ++ (List.ofFn (fun g => pack (gen g))).flatten ++
          pack u ++ pack v ++ pack cr ++ pack cc ++ List.ofFn (fun targetIndex => decide (target targetIndex ≠ 0))
        H.rank ≤ q →
        let count := Nat.card { w : W // w ∈ Set.range key ∧ ∀ j, probe w j = target j }
        ∀ o : Fin (k+1), (C.wires bits).getD (out o).val false = count.testBit o.val
changed.unlocks: Counts exact fibers on affine key families even when the cyclic boundary realizes exponentially many words.
changed.context: Sample each probe at zero, unit vectors and pairs to recover its multilinear coefficients. Row-reduce the quadratic parts, carrying the linear and constant terms. The zero rows are affine equations. Solve them and parametrize their common flat. For the h remaining rows use character orthogonality with 2^h signs. Evaluate each signed quadratic sum by eliminating xy+xA+yB to a factor two and sign AB, or eliminate an isolated variable directly. Divide by 2^h and by the generator kernel size to count distinct keys.

Divide by 2^h and by the generator kernel size to count distinct keys.

changed.title: Mask weights bound the polar rank and affine correlation of combined one-round cyclic row and column outputs
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 11 ≤ k →
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let ix := fun pos : ℕ => (⟨pos % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (j : Fin k) => w (ix (j.val+k-s%k))
  let run := fun (d s f : ℕ) (w name c : W) =>
    let z := rot s w + name
    let y := fun mid : Fin k => z mid + z (ix (mid.val+d)) + z (ix (mid.val+k-d%k))
    fun siteOut : Fin k => y siteOut + (1+y (ix (siteOut.val+1))) * y (ix (siteOut.val+2)) + rot f w siteOut + c siteOut
  ∀ (u v cr cc a b : W),
    let F := fun raw : W => dotProduct a (run 1 1 0 raw u cr) + dotProduct b (run 2 3 4 raw v cc)
    let unit := fun (j i : Fin k) => (if i = j then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2)
    let P : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) (ZMod 2) := fun left right =>
      F (unit left + unit right) + F (unit left) + F (unit right) + F 0
    let wt := fun mask : W => (Finset.univ.filter (fun index => mask index ≠ 0)).card
    let r := P.rank
    (k-10)*wt b ≤ k*r ∧ (k-6)*wt a ≤ k*(r+2*wt b) ∧
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (hs : s ≤ k) (L : (Fin s → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] W), Function.Injective L →
      ∀ (base : W) (ell : (Fin s → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2) (c : ZMod 2),
        let bias := ∑ x : Fin s → ZMod 2,
          (if F (base + L x) + ell x + c = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1)
        bias^2 * (2 : ℤ)^(r-2*(k-s)) ≤ (2 : ℤ)^(2*s)
changed.unlocks: Bounds affine prediction of both tests together and detects when quadratic dependencies require restricting the key family.
changed.context: In the joint polar matrix the entry at raw sites i−4,i+1 equals column mask bit b_i. Every entry at cyclic distance above five vanishes. In a cyclic interval of k−10 anchors the marked entries form the diagonal of a triangular minor. Average over its translates. The row-only matrix has radius three and outer entries a_i, giving the k−6 bound. Each selected column contributes polar rank at most two. Restriction to codimension c loses at most 2c rank. Apply the quadratic Walsh radical formula on the flat.

Apply the quadratic Walsh radical formula on the flat.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: Lokam’s rank bound for every rectangular submatrix of a real Hadamard matrix
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ (a b : ℕ) (rows : Fin a ↪ Fin n) (cols : Fin b ↪ Fin n),
    a * b ≤ n * (H.submatrix rows cols).rank
changed.unlocks: Bounds the clean rectangle in an edited sign table.
changed.context: The selected matrix has squared Frobenius norm ab. Restricting to rows and columns cannot raise the operator norm above the square root of n. Sum the squares of its nonzero singular values.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: Lowering a real Hadamard matrix to rank at most r requires at least n²/(4r) changed entries
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < r → 2*r ≤ n → A.rank ≤ r →
    let changes := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)).filter (fun p => H p.1 p.2 ≠ A p.1 p.2)
    n^2 ≤ 4*r*changes.card
changed.unlocks: Prices edits that destroy the rank of a sign table.
changed.context: Write D for the number of changed cells. Select 2r rows with at most 2rD/n changes, then discard columns hit by those changes. The remaining rectangle equals a submatrix of H and its rank is at most r. Apply the submatrix rank bound and rearrange.
changed.sketch: Write D for the number of changed cells. Select 2r rows with at most 2rD/n changes, then discard columns hit by those changes. The remaining rectangle equals a submatrix of H and its rank is at most r. Apply the submatrix rank bound and rearrange.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: Normalized row overlaps with a Hadamard basis sum to at most the approximant rank
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
    (∑ i, (∑ j, H i j * A i j)^2 / (∑ j, (A i j)^2)) ≤ (n : ℝ) * (A.rank : ℝ)
changed.unlocks: Controls accuracy after each predictor row is normalized separately.
changed.context: Project each orthonormal row of H divided by the square root of n onto the row space of A. Its squared overlap with the corresponding normalized A row is at most this projected squared length. The sum of all projected squared lengths is the dimension of the row space.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: The bounded rigidity inequality for real Hadamard matrices
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (θ : ℝ), 0 ≤ θ →
    (∀ i j, |H i j - A i j| ≤ θ) →
    let D := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)).filter (fun p => H p.1 p.2 ≠ A p.1 p.2)).card
    (n : ℝ)^2 * ((n : ℝ) - (A.rank : ℝ)) ≤
      (D : ℝ) * (2*θ*n + (A.rank : ℝ)*(θ^2+2*θ))
changed.unlocks: Prices edits whose amplitudes have a fixed ceiling.
changed.context: For each approximant row bound its squared norm by n+d(θ²+2θ), where d is its error count. Its normalized squared overlap with the target row is bounded below by (n-2θd)/(n+d(θ²+2θ)), also when that numerator is negative. The function of d is convex. Average and apply the normalized-row overlap bound, treating zero rows separately.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: Forster’s sign-rank lower bound for a real Hadamard sign pattern
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →

Its spectral estimate gives r at least n divided by the spectral norm of the sign matrix. Orthogonality makes the latter the square root of n.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: The finite support uncertainty inequality for a real Hadamard transform
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, x ≠ 0 →

      (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => y i ≠ 0)).card

changed.context: Orthogonality gives squared output norm n times squared input norm. Every output coordinate has magnitude at most the square root of the input support size times the input norm. Sum only over the output support and cancel the positive squared input norm.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: The Welch bound for the total squared correlations of unit vectors
changed.statement:
∀ (n k : ℕ) (v : Fin k → Fin n → ℝ),

    (k : ℝ)^2 ≤ (n : ℝ) * ∑ a, ∑ b, (dot (v a) (v b))^2

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. A weighted automaton has a prefix-closed basis of reachable states
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q d : ℕ),
  let V := Fin d → K
  ∀ (s : V) (A : Fin q → V →ₗ[K] V),
    let run := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun x a => A a x) s
    ∃ P : Finset (List (Fin q)), P.card ≤ d ∧
      (∀ w ∈ P, w.length < d) ∧ (∀ w a, w ++ [a] ∈ P → w ∈ P) ∧
      LinearIndependent K (fun w : P => run w.val) ∧
      ∀ w, run w ∈ Submodule.span K (run '' (↑P : Set (List (Fin q))))
changed.unlocks: gives a short prefix basis for exact weighted counter states
changed.context: If the initial vector is zero use the empty set. Otherwise start with the empty word. For each retained word test its one-letter extensions and retain each vector outside the span so far. Dimension bounds insertions by d. When no extension escapes, linearity makes the span invariant and induction reaches every word. Each insertion has a retained parent, so a word of length h needs at least h+1 retained words.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Inequivalent weighted automata have a distinguishing word shorter than their combined dimension
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q d e : ℕ),
  let V := Fin d → K
  let W := Fin e → K
  ∀ (s : V) (t : W) (A : Fin q → V →ₗ[K] V) (B : Fin q → W →ₗ[K] W)
    (f : V →ₗ[K] K) (g : W →ₗ[K] K),
    let X := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun x a => A a x) s
    let Y := fun (w : List (Fin q)) => w.foldl (fun y a => B a y) t
    (∃ w, f (X w) ≠ g (Y w)) →
      ∃ w, w.length < d + e ∧ f (X w) ≠ g (Y w)
changed.unlocks: bounds a distinguishing input length by the combined state dimension
changed.context: Run both systems in the direct sum and subtract their terminal functionals. Its dimension is d+e. A basis of reachable states is generated by words shorter than d+e. If the difference vanishes on every basis vector, linearity makes it vanish on every word. This also handles a zero-dimensional system.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Finite Hankel rank characterizes the dimension of a weighted automaton realization
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q : ℕ) (f : List (Fin q) → K),
  let R := Submodule.span K (Set.range (fun u : List (Fin q) => fun v : List (Fin q) => f (u ++ v)))
  ∀ d : ℕ, (Module.Finite K R ∧ Module.finrank K R ≤ d) ↔
    ∃ (s : Fin d → K) (A : Fin q → (Fin d → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin d → K))
      (g : (Fin d → K) →ₗ[K] K),
      ∀ w : List (Fin q), g (w.foldl (fun x a => A a x) s) = f w

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. A full-rank Hankel minor and its one-letter extensions reconstruct every word value
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (q : ℕ) (f : List (Fin q) → K),
  let R := Submodule.span K (Set.range (fun u : List (Fin q) => fun v : List (Fin q) => f (u ++ v)))
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (U V : Fin r → List (Fin q)),
    Module.Finite K R → Module.finrank K R = r →
    let H := Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin r => f (U i ++ V j))
    H.det ≠ 0 →
    let B := fun a : Fin q =>
      Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin r => f (U i ++ [a] ++ V j)) * H⁻¹
    ∀ w : List (Fin q), f w =
      dotProduct (Matrix.vecMul (fun j => f (V j)) H⁻¹)
        (Matrix.mulVec ((w.map B).prod) (fun i => f (U i)))
changed.unlocks: reconstructs the transition matrices from accessible prefix and suffix samples
changed.context: The selected residuals are independent, so they form a basis. Values on the pivot suffixes give a row of samples. right multiplication by the inverse Hankel block converts it to basis coordinates. Apply this to each basis residual after extending its prefix by one letter. The empty-prefix sample row initializes the representation, and the values at the empty suffix give its terminal column. Multiply in word order.
